email.subject: Your new insurance card: please check your details

body.v: Please find attached your new insurance card for next year. Kindly open it and check that your details are correct.
Cards that have not been confirmed will be blocked on 1 January.

hotspots.explain: Read the domain from the right: the owner is card-service.example. The helveticare.example in front of it is just scenery.
"blocked on 1 January": a threat with a date on it, so you open the file without waiting.
"insurance-card.jpg.html" ends in .html: it is a web page dressed up as a picture, and it would show a fake sign-in page.
Your first name is easy to find. It proves nothing.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Someone using HelvetiCare's name. The address actually belongs to card-service.example.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: Fear and haste: your card will be blocked on 1 January if you do nothing.
choices: None, it is a routine mailing
Fear of a blocked card, on a set date

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Open the attachment. The file is a web page that would harvest your login details.
choices: Reply with your date of birth
Open the attachment and check your details

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Do not open it. Check your card in the HelvetiCare app, or call the number printed on your current card.
choices: Open the file to see what it is
Reply to ask for the card in another format
Call the number on your card, or use the app

actions.label: Call the number on your current card and ask about the new one
actions.consequence: They tell you no new card is on its way. The email was fake.

actions.label: Open the attachment to check your details
actions.consequence: A fake sign-in page opens. Whatever you type there goes to the scammer.

actions.label: Reply to ask for the card in another format
actions.consequence: The scammer sends you another file, and now knows your address is active.

actions.label: Report it as phishing and delete it
actions.consequence: The file was never opened, and it never will be.

attacker_reveal: ".jpg", and most people stop reading there. Yet the last extension is the one that tells the browser what to do, and mine was .html. Put a date on the threat and people click before they have finished reading.
